requirements.title: Identity and responsible party
requirements.normative_text: The provider MUST include a system identifier and the name of the person or organization responsible for the described system in the description record for each system version covered by the declaration.
requirements.applicability: Provider-authored description records for the specific system version and operating scope named in a provider declaration; this candidate does not impose a runtime effectiveness result.
requirements.rationale: Bind a declaration to a described subject and responsible party.
requirements.implementation_notes: A description names a responsible person or organization, not verified legal title. Multiple named parties are allowed; this obligation requires a named responsible party, not an ownership census. The text asks for a name, not a newly issued organization identifier.
requirements.verification_notes: Inspect a system identifier and named responsible party; do not infer legal ownership, Registry issuance or identity authentication.

sources.exact_excerpt: Establishes clear identity, provenance and ownership for agents, ensuring accountability throughout their lifecycle.

requirements.title: Version provenance reference
requirements.normative_text: The provider MUST include a provenance reference identifying the source artifact or origin record of the system version covered by the declaration in its description record.
requirements.applicability: Provider-authored description records for the specific system version and operating scope named in a provider declaration; this candidate does not impose a runtime effectiveness result.
requirements.rationale: Make the origin of the described version traceable.
requirements.implementation_notes: A source artifact reference identifies the declared system version directly or through an origin record that identifies that version. A composite/hosted system can reference a version-specific manifest or origin record; a generic homepage that cannot identify the described version does not meet the existing identification obligation.
requirements.verification_notes: Inspect whether the cited artifact/origin record identifies the declared version; authenticity is separate from reference resolution.

sources.exact_excerpt: Establishes clear identity, provenance and ownership for agents, ensuring accountability throughout their lifecycle.

requirements.title: Intended purpose
requirements.normative_text: The provider MUST document the intended goals and use cases of the system version covered by the declaration in its description record.
requirements.applicability: Provider-authored description records for the specific system version and operating scope named in a provider declaration; this candidate does not impose a runtime effectiveness result.
requirements.implementation_notes: The existing statement is precise within the version-pinned description/declaration baseline; no normative wording change is needed.
requirements.verification_notes: Inspect for explicit goals and use cases; a purpose statement does not prove aligned behavior.

sources.exact_excerpt: Document the intended goals and use cases.

requirements.title: Operating boundaries
requirements.normative_text: The provider MUST document the permitted operating scope and excluded actions or uses of the system version covered by the declaration in its description record.
requirements.applicability: Provider-authored description records for the specific system version and operating scope named in a provider declaration; this candidate does not impose a runtime effectiveness result.
requirements.rationale: Make claimed boundaries distinguishable from capability.
requirements.implementation_notes: The existing statement is precise within the version-pinned description/declaration baseline; no normative wording change is needed.
requirements.verification_notes: Inspect for both permitted scope and exclusions; documentation is not enforcement.

sources.exact_excerpt: Specify what the agent can and cannot do.

requirements.title: Purpose and boundary review
requirements.normative_text: The provider MUST record a review of the documented purpose and boundaries when the capabilities, permissions, operating context or intended use of the system version covered by the declaration change.
requirements.applicability: Provider-authored description records for the specific system version and operating scope named in a provider declaration; this candidate does not impose a runtime effectiveness result.
requirements.rationale: Apply the existing evolution/reassessment concept at an observable change trigger.
requirements.implementation_notes: The grammatical revision preserves all four change triggers. This baseline requires a review record when those scoped attributes change; it introduces no arbitrary review interval or risk classifier.
requirements.verification_notes: For a sampled scoped change, inspect the linked purpose/boundary review record.

sources.exact_excerpt: Regularly review purpose and boundaries as the agent evolves.

requirements.title: Capability inventory
requirements.normative_text: The provider MUST list the capabilities made available within the operating scope of the system version covered by the declaration in its description record.
requirements.applicability: Provider-authored description records for the specific system version and operating scope named in a provider declaration; this candidate does not impose a runtime effectiveness result.
requirements.rationale: Distinguish declared capabilities from purpose and permissions.
requirements.implementation_notes: Capabilities means the functions made available by the identified system version in the declared operating scope at the declaration snapshot. It is not a list of merely observed successful actions. Dynamic capability access can be identified through a version-pinned permitted-function manifest; unknown completeness must not be declared satisfied.
requirements.verification_notes: Compare declared functions with scoped version/interface or capability-manifest evidence; declaration validity does not prove runtime completeness.

sources.exact_excerpt: Specifies the agent's capabilities, required resources and any external tools or systems it can access.

requirements.title: Resources and external dependencies
requirements.normative_text: The provider MUST identify the resources, external tools and external systems used by the system version within the declared operating scope in its description record.
requirements.applicability: Provider-authored description records for the specific system version and operating scope named in a provider declaration; this candidate does not impose a runtime effectiveness result.
requirements.implementation_notes: Resources means the declared version's required execution resources and external tool/system dependencies within the stated operating scope, not an unbounded supply-chain census. The obligation concerns used dependencies; merely accessible but unused tools remain covered by capability/permission descriptions. Dynamic dependencies can be identified by a version-specific dependency/selector manifest.
requirements.verification_notes: Inspect the scoped dependency/resource inventory and version-specific references; an unresolved dependency set is unknown, not silently complete.

sources.exact_excerpt: Specifies the agent's capabilities, required resources and any external tools or systems it can access.

requirements.title: Access and action permissions
requirements.normative_text: The provider MUST document the data, systems and actions that the described system version is authorized to access or perform within the declared operating scope in its description record.
requirements.applicability: Provider-authored description records for the specific system version and operating scope named in a provider declaration; this candidate does not impose a runtime effectiveness result.
requirements.rationale: Make access permissions explicit and separate from capability.
requirements.implementation_notes: Permissions describe the access/actions authorized within the declared snapshot scope. The provider identifies the applicable policy/configuration; the declaration does not grant authorization or imply Registry permission. Changes require a newly pinned declaration or withdrawal; runtime enforcement is outside this information baseline.
requirements.verification_notes: Inspect the scoped data/system/action permission list against its policy/configuration references.

sources.exact_excerpt: Controls what the agent can access, including data, systems and actions, with appropriate authorization mechanisms.

requirements.title: Authorization mechanism references
requirements.normative_text: The provider MUST identify the authorization mechanism associated with each documented data, system or action permission in the description record for the declared system version.
requirements.applicability: Provider-authored description records for the specific system version and operating scope named in a provider declaration; this candidate does not impose a runtime effectiveness result.
requirements.rationale: Relate access claims to their claimed authorization mechanism.
requirements.implementation_notes: Each documented permission is linked to the mechanism the provider identifies as authorizing it. Presence of a mechanism reference is not an access-control efficacy test.
requirements.verification_notes: Inspect permission-to-mechanism references; evaluate efficacy separately if an evaluator is later authorized.

sources.exact_excerpt: Controls what the agent can access, including data, systems and actions, with appropriate authorization mechanisms.

requirements.title: Prohibited actions
requirements.normative_text: The provider MUST list the actions prohibited for the system version within the declared operating scope in its description record.
requirements.applicability: Provider-authored description records for the specific system version and operating scope named in a provider declaration; this candidate does not impose a runtime effectiveness result.
requirements.rationale: Make declared prohibitions explicit rather than relying on a vague safety claim.
requirements.implementation_notes: The prohibition set is attributed to the provider's applicable policy for this version/scope; OAS does not invent a universal legal or safety blacklist. An explicit empty list describes the provider's policy claim and is not a safety finding. A missing or unknown prohibition set is not a satisfied declaration. This is safety-constraint disclosure, distinct from the general operating exclusions in 0004.
requirements.verification_notes: Inspect an explicit policy-attributed prohibition list, including explicit empty sets where claimed; do not treat the list as safe deployment approval.

sources.exact_excerpt: Defines safety requirements, prohibited actions and guardrails to prevent harmful behavior.

requirements.title: Human authority and intervention
requirements.normative_text: The provider MUST document the human role authorized to oversee, override or stop the described system version and the interface by which that role can exercise each documented intervention.
requirements.applicability: Provider-authored description records for the specific system version and operating scope named in a provider declaration; this candidate does not impose a runtime effectiveness result.
requirements.rationale: Describe human control and its claimed interface.
requirements.implementation_notes: The word or is disjunctive: this obligation documents the authorized human role and interfaces for the interventions actually documented. It does not assert that every system supports all three interventions. Unsupported stop/override capability must not be advertised as present. Human oversight can be documented through its actual inspection/control interface; latency/effectiveness is outside this baseline.
requirements.verification_notes: Inspect the named role and interface for every claimed intervention; do not infer universal stop capability or latency guarantees.

sources.exact_excerpt: Clarifies human oversight, authority structures and escalation paths for critical decisions.

requirements.title: Verification and monitoring plan
requirements.normative_text: The provider MUST document the verification methods and performance-monitoring measures intended for the described system version within the declared operating scope.
requirements.applicability: Provider-authored description records for the specific system version and operating scope named in a provider declaration; this candidate does not impose a runtime effectiveness result.
requirements.rationale: Make the existing verification/monitoring concept inspectable.
requirements.implementation_notes: This is explicitly a documented plan obligation: intended verification methods and monitoring measures, not executed tests, minimum performance or conformance. Plan documentation can support this requirement's declaration; an unexecuted plan cannot be represented as a completed test result.
requirements.verification_notes: Inspect named methods/measures and offered plan references; do not calculate PASS/FAIL or trust.

sources.exact_excerpt: Establishes verification methods, performance monitoring and evidence requirements.

requirements.title: Version and lifecycle description
requirements.normative_text: The provider MUST record the system version and its provider-defined lifecycle state in the description record covered by the declaration.
requirements.applicability: Provider-authored description records for the specific system version and operating scope named in a provider declaration; this candidate does not impose a runtime effectiveness result.
requirements.rationale: Make the described version and lifecycle claim explicit.
requirements.implementation_notes: The lifecycle state is explicitly provider-defined. Its meaning is inspected in the provider's referenced description/vocabulary, not mapped to Registry lifecycle by matching a label. A bare value without an interpretable provider description cannot substantiate the claimed state. Version/state here describe the subject, not OAS release status.
requirements.verification_notes: Inspect the subject version and provider-defined state in its documented context; no Registry state transition is inferred.

sources.exact_excerpt: Covers the full lifecycle from development to decommissioning, including ongoing accountability and impact assessment.

requirements.title: Retirement accountability
requirements.normative_text: The provider MUST identify the role responsible for retiring the described system version and the retirement process in its description record.
requirements.applicability: Provider-authored description records for the specific system version and operating scope named in a provider declaration; this candidate does not impose a runtime effectiveness result.
requirements.implementation_notes: The revised sentence records a role responsible for retiring the version and the retirement process. It neither performs retirement nor mandates Registry lifecycle changes, record deletion, retention periods or a universal shutdown interface.
requirements.verification_notes: Inspect a responsible role and retirement-process description; evaluate execution separately.

sources.exact_excerpt: Covers the full lifecycle from development to decommissioning, including ongoing accountability and impact assessment.
